## Install

The following packages must be installed

* readr
* ggplot2
* dplyr

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

```

## Pre-Features

Examines some trends in the data prior to any additional feature creation. Note that for day of the week Sunday = 0 and Sat = 6.

```{r}

set.seed(42)

# read in all files as one data set
files <- list.files(path = "labeled_data/", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE, recursive=TRUE)

fullDF <- read_csv(files, id = "source_file")

# print # of unique meters, shoudl be 100
length(unique(fullDF$meter_num))

# num rows matches expected intervals for 100 meters
nrow(fullDF) == 100*((365*24*4)-3)

# create month and day attribute for grouping
fullDF$start_full = as.POSIXct(fullDF$start_full, format = "%m-%d-%Y %H:%M")
fullDF$month = format(fullDF$start_full, "%m")
fullDF$day = format(fullDF$start_full, "%w")

# grab a single random meter
singleMeter = sample(unique(fullDF$meter_num), 1)

```

### Usage by Month

Compare a single meter's yearly usage by month to the total of all accounts. Both a random single meter and an aggregate of all meters show a trend based on time of the year. Higher values in peak heating and cooling seasons, lower in "shoulder" months where heating/cooling not used as much. 

Filtering by EV accounts this trend is less pronounced but does still exist. 

```{r}

meterDF = fullDF[fullDF$meter_num == singleMeter, ]

# graph usage grouped by month - https://stackoverflow.com/questions/60377831/sum-of-variables-in-a-grouped-barplot-in-ggplot2
aggDF = aggregate(value ~ month, data=meterDF, FUN='sum')

aggDF %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = value))+
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + 
  labs(title="Single Meter Annual Usage By Month", x="kWh", y="Month")

```

```{r}
# aggregate all accounts, generate same graph, filter EV or non EV if needed
aggDF = aggregate(value ~ month, data=fullDF, FUN='sum')
#aggDF = aggregate(value ~ month, data=fullDF[fullDF$EV == TRUE, ], FUN='sum')

aggDF %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = value))+
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + 
  labs(title="All Meters Annual Usage By Month", x="kWh", y="Month")
```

### Usage By Day 

Broken down by day usage is fairly flat over days of the week. A slight uptick on weekends but no clear trend.

```{r}

# aggregate all accounts, filter EV or non EV if needed
aggDF = aggregate(value ~ day, data=fullDF, FUN='sum')
#aggDF = aggregate(value ~ day, data=fullDF[fullDF$EV == FALSE, ], FUN='sum')

aggDF %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = day, y = value))+
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + 
  labs(title="All Meters Annual Usage By Day Of Week", x="kWh", y="Day Of Week")

```
